title: Violence and abandonment

blocks.heading: Violence and abandonment
blocks.text: Gender-based violence concerns harmful acts linked to gender and unequal power; infant abandonment is a distinct child-protection issue. Discuss interacting social risks and barriers to support without treating poverty or household type as proof of violence or abandonment. Responsibility for violence rests with the perpetrator, not the survivor.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: GBV-related factors
blocks.text: Unequal power, norms tolerating abuse, coercion and barriers to effective support can contribute to gender-based violence. Risk factors are not excuses or a prediction about an individual. An educational discussion should not request learners’ personal experiences or expose someone’s identity.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Infant abandonment factors
blocks.text: Crisis, fear, stigma, coercion, isolation and difficulty reaching trusted support can interact around unsafe infant abandonment. No single factor explains a particular case, and young or poor parents should not be labelled as likely offenders. Focus on protection and accessible qualified support, without providing unsafe instructions.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: A practical access test
blocks.text: Explain the access mechanism in this fictional case: a fictional support centre receives few requests while travel is unaffordable and users fear public identification. Low recorded use may reflect access and privacy barriers rather than low need. A safe reachable arrangement addresses those mechanisms without inferring individual cases.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Protection is a coordinated task
blocks.text: Namibia’s 2012–2016 GBV plan, documented by [UNDP](https://www.undp.org/namibia/publications/namibia-national-plan-gender-based-violence-gbv-2012-2016), combined prevention, service implementation and survivor support, including a distinct infant-abandonment concern. This is a dated example. [UNICEF Namibia](https://www.unicef.org/namibia/child-protection) describes child protection through supportive family, community and institutional environments. Checked 20 October 2026; no current hotline or legal procedure is asserted.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
blocks.text: Connect to traditional roles (6.1), education (7.3) and research (10.1). Use evidence about resources, voice and practical access. Fictional cases do not establish current law, service availability or a diagnosis about any individual.
